sections.description: This section focuses on the patient's initial presentation, the timeline of symptom development, and the critical distinction between the acute drug reaction and the subacute development of myopathy.
subtopics: Initial adverse reactions to semaglutide: Gastrointestinal symptoms and acute renal failure
The subacute phase: Progressive proximal muscle weakness and bulbar symptoms (dysphagia and dysphonia)
Temporal relationship between GLP-1 receptor agonist administration and the onset of muscle weakness
Baseline comorbidities and their relevance (obesity, NAFLD, and hypertension)

sections.description: This section provides the necessary medical background to understand IMNM, contrasting it with other forms of muscle injury and explaining the underlying mechanisms of the disease.
subtopics: Defining IMNM: Characteristics of necrotising myofibres and inflammatory infiltrates
Autoantibody profiles: The role of anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibodies
Seronegative IMNM: Diagnostic challenges and potential triggers
Distinguishing IMNM from toxic rhabdomyolysis: Kinetics of CK elevation and recovery patterns

sections.description: This section details the multimodal approach used to reach the diagnosis, explaining how laboratory data, imaging, and histology were synthesized.
subtopics: Biochemical markers: Interpreting severe CK elevation and transaminase levels
Imaging modalities: Role of muscle MRI in detecting edema and cardiac MRI in assessing myocardial inflammation
The gold standard: Muscle biopsy findings (necrosis, regeneration, and CD68/MAC staining)
Screening for systemic involvement: Evaluating interstitial lung disease and cardiac function

sections.description: This section explores the clinical logic used to rule out other possibilities and the methodology used to link the myopathy to semaglutide use.
subtopics: Differentiating hepatic vs. muscular origin of elevated transaminases
Evaluating the significance of isolated SS-B positivity in the absence of ANA and SS-A
Comparison with other GLP-1 receptor agonist cases (e.g., tirzepatide-induced rhabdomyolysis)
Application of the WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) Causality Categories

sections.description: The final section covers the treatment strategy, the patient's recovery process, and the broader implications for pharmacological safety and monitoring.
subtopics: Immunosuppressive therapy: Pulse methylprednisolone, oral prednisone, and IVIG
Treatment response: Monitoring CK levels and functional recovery
The importance of drug withdrawal and avoidance of GLP-1 receptor agonists in recovery
Clinical lessons for pharmacovigilance in the era of increasing GLP-1 receptor agonist use
